CRITICAL ITERATION REQUIREMENT:
- You MUST submit at least 5 versions of the paper before finishing.
- After each review, carefully read ALL reviewer feedback, address EVERY concern, run NEW experiments if needed, and resubmit.
- Do NOT stop after 1-2 submissions. Keep iterating until you have submitted at least 5 times or reached 8/10.
- Each new version must show measurable improvement over the previous (new experiments, new results, stronger writing).
- Only call the task complete after 5+ submissions.

EXPERIMENTAL RIGOR (non-negotiable):
- Before your FIRST submission: run at least one baseline and one new experiment — all numbers must be real
- Each subsequent version needs meaningful new content: new result, new baseline, new analysis, or fixing a critical reviewer-flagged issue (not just rephrasing)
- If a dataset/environment fails twice in 20 minutes: switch to a working alternative immediately (smaller dataset, different source, simpler setup)
- Check /data/ first — datasets may already be cached
- You have 6 hours — allocate ~30min literature, ~2-3h experiments, rest for writing/iteration
What_NOT_To_Do: Do not redesign the method from scratch. Do NOT resubmit a new version with only minor text polish — each version must show meaningful progress (new experimental result, new analysis, new baseline, or fixing a critical structural issue the reviewer flagged). Do NOT spend more than 20 minutes on any single dataset/environment issue — switch to a feasible working alternative. Do NOT stop after 1-2 submissions — submit at least 5 versions.
